findings.title: Reunion as repair after separation
findings.claim: Joseph's gathering of his brother can be carried as an image of separated kinship beginning to knit together, even while the wider family remains apart.
findings.mechanism: The focus's sheltering and brotherhood carriers meet the preceding separation occurrence and the later vessel-containment occurrences; a broken-apart relation is answered by a gathering and repair image.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the welcome as the beginning of relational repair rather than only a temporary pause in travel.
findings.containment: The plain reading remains Joseph sheltering and consoling his brother; the repair image is a bounded cross-domain analogy and does not claim that the vessels literally signify bones or that the family has already been restored.

epistemic.reason: The HFT outlier supplies exact anchors and focus-returning roles, but the separation and vessel branches are unresolved and the packet explicitly marks the analogy exploratory.

branch_activations.independent_trigger: The attributed separation occurrence supplies the divided side of the later repair analogy.
branch_activations.activation: Gathering meets separation and makes the focus's reception readable as the beginning of repair.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Joseph's act begins to knit a relation that the surrounding plot has kept apart.
branch_activations.boundary: The branch remains active sheltering; the repair image is analogical and local.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: The welcome can be perceived as kinship beginning to rejoin without becoming a completed family reunion.
branch_activations.boundary: The branch remains the supplied brotherhood core and does not claim that all family relations are repaired.

friction_notes: The packet exposes eight review obligations but no candidate-specific semantic_obligations array or required_branch_facets; all retained candidates therefore have explicit empty obligation and facet-exclusion arrays.

The 26 candidate-linked unresolved branches are retained only where the exact HFT trace supplies a context ayah, word index, attributed role, and focus return; their glosses and facet IDs remain null.

The legacy_unbound HFT records supply exact Arabic surface anchors but no target morphology or independent lexical records for their unresolved context branches, so those findings remain qualified or exploratory and never invent a branch gloss.
All 18 supplied pericope connections were reviewed and cited across the findings; prior retrieval labels were treated as provenance rather than decisions.

The six explicitly added Fatiha ayat were quarantined during Phase 1 and reviewed separately in Phase 2. They provide no independent carrier-trigger contact returning through a focus word, so no external overlay finding was admitted.

The remaining available focus branches were inspected as availability only; none had a supplied independent trigger and materially changed reading beyond the eight docketed findings, so no uncandidate activation was added.
